title: Apprenticeship Degrees: Earning College Credit on the Job
description: Apprenticeship degrees let a learner earn a paycheck, a journey-level credential, and college credit at the same time. This course explains the models (credit for related instruction, credit for prior learning, degree-embedded apprenticeships), California's current examples including teacher apprenticeships under AB 1904, and how to advise participants who want both a career and a degree.
notes: Audience: Career specialists, youth staff, education partners. Format: LV or SP. Hours assumed from format (LV/SP = 3 hours). Track note: California's apprenticeship-degree landscape is early. AB 1904 (credentialed educator apprenticeships) and the Chancellor's Office Apprenticeship Pathway Demonstration Project are the anchors; a CSU or Apprenticeship Degree Network footprint was not verified. These courses should be refreshed as the field develops.
learning_objectives: Explain how apprenticeship hours and related instruction can convert to college credit.
Describe California's current apprenticeship-degree models and their requirements.
Advise a participant comparing a traditional degree, an apprenticeship, and an apprenticeship degree on cost, time, and earnings.
Identify how WIOA training funds and ETPL rules apply to degree-linked apprenticeships.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: How Apprenticeship Converts to College Credit; California's Apprenticeship-Degree Models; Advising: Degree, Apprenticeship, or Both; WIOA Training Funds and the ETPL for Degree-Linked Apprenticeships. There is no separate project lesson; each lesson ends in a practice exercise built on the same running case. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (LV or SP; LV/SP = 3 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Track caveat: California's apprenticeship-degree landscape is early. AB 1904 (credentialed educator apprenticeships) and the Chancellor's Office Apprenticeship Pathway Demonstration Project are the anchors; a CSU or Apprenticeship Degree Network footprint was not verified. These courses should be refreshed as the field develops. Prerequisites reflect track order: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals).
